methods.name: to_dict
methods.summary: Return the config as the JSON-ready dict `adapter_config.json` holds.
methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.  A field the reference's config of this method lacks
(`IA3Config.layers_to_transform`) is written only when it is set,
so a file that does not use it is one the reference reads too.

returns.description: One entry per field, keyed by the reference's field names.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> d = LoraConfig(target_modules=["v", "q"], task_type="CAUSAL_LM").to_dict()
>>> d["target_modules"], d["task_type"], d["peft_type"]
(['q', 'v'], 'CAUSAL_LM', 'LORA')

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"loftq_config": {}`, `"megatron_config": null`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is dropped.  Called on
`PeftConfig`, the dict's `peft_type` picks the class.

parameters.name: config_dict
parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class the dict's method names.

raises.description:
The dict describes another adapter type, or turns on a feature
v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.summary: Write `adapter_config.json` into `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
The file is the reference's: `to_dict` with its keys sorted,
indented by two spaces.  The directory is created if missing.

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
`auto_mapping_dict` replaces the `auto_mapping` the file records.
The reference forwards any other keyword to its hub upload; there
is no hub here, so another key raises.

raises.description: `save_directory` names an existing file.
`kwargs` holds a key other than `auto_mapping_dict`.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d).r
2

methods.name: from_json_file
methods.summary: Read a config file into the dict it holds, unchanged but for `runtime_config`.
methods.extended:
What `from_pretrained` reads before it chooses a config class: the
file's content as a dict, as the reference's `from_json_file` returns
it.  `from_dict` turns it into a config.

parameters.name: path_json_file
parameters.description: The path of a JSON file such as `adapter_config.json`.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
Accepted for the reference's signature; it passes none to the
reader, and any key given here raises.

returns.description:
The file's object, without a `runtime_config` key: the
reference warns that such a key is ignored, since a runtime
configuration is valid at runtime only.

raises.description: There is no file at `path_json_file`.
The file does not hold a JSON object.
`kwargs` is not empty.

examples:
>>> import os, tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     raw = PeftConfig.from_json_file(os.path.join(d, "adapter_config.json"))
>>> raw["peft_type"], raw["r"]
('LORA', 2)

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(pretrained_model_name_or_path: str | os.PathLike[str], subfolder: str | None = None, kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Read `adapter_config.json` from a local adapter directory.
methods.extended:
The file's `peft_type` picks the config class: called on
`PeftConfig` this returns a `LoraConfig` for a LoRA adapter,
and called on a method's own class it refuses the file of another
method.

A directory holding `adapter_config.json` — one written by
`save_pretrained` or by the reference library.  Hub ids
are not resolved; download the adapter first.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description:
A directory under `pretrained_model_name_or_path` that holds
the file, e.g. the sub-directory `save_pretrained` gives each
adapter but the one named `"default"`.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub download (`revision`,
`token`, `cache_dir` …).  Adapters are read from a local
directory, so any key given here raises.

raises.description: The directory has no `adapter_config.json`.
The file does not hold a JSON object.
`kwargs` is not empty.

>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules="all-linear").save_pretrained(d)
...     loaded = LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d)
>>> loaded.r, loaded.lora_alpha, loaded.target_modules
(16, 32, 'all-linear')

members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with C3A.
members.extended:
C3A (Chen et al., 2024, [arXiv:2407.19342](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19342) — Circular Convolution Adaptation) makes the
weight update a **block-circulant matrix**: the $d_{out} \times d_{in}$ update is
cut into $b \times b$ blocks and each block is a circulant, fixed by its first row
— a length-$b$ kernel.  The layer trains $d_{out} d_{in} / b$ numbers
($b$ kernels per block row and column), which is high rank, and applies them by
FFT without building the matrix,

$$

$$

With `init_weights=True` the kernels start at zero and the adapted model is the base;
the default is a Xavier-uniform sample (non-zero).  The update folds into the weight.

Field names, their order, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference adapter
library's.

parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.name: peft_type
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.name: block_size
parameters.description:
The block size $b$; it must divide both of a layer's sizes.  Larger blocks
mean fewer parameters.  The greatest common divisor of all the targeted layers' sizes
is the largest that fits them all.

parameters.name: target_modules
parameters.description:
The `nn.Linear` modules to adapt, matched as `LoraConfig.target_modules`
is.  `None` takes the LoRA default for the base model's `model_type`, with `gpt2`
narrowed to `mlp.c_proj` as the reference does.

parameters.name: bias
parameters.description:
The reference also offers `"all"` and `"c3a_only"`; here the adapter trains its
kernels only, and those raise `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: modules_to_save
parameters.description: Modules trained in full beside the adapter (a classifier head).

parameters.name: layers_to_transform
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraConfig`.

parameters.name: layers_pattern
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraConfig`.

parameters.name: block_size_pattern
parameters.description: Per-module `block_size` overrides, keyed by name or regex suffix.

parameters.name: init_weights
parameters.description: `True`: zeros.  `False`: as `"xavier_uniform"`.  A name picks that sampler.

parameters.name: exclude_modules
parameters.description: Modules never adapted, matched like `target_modules`.

raises.description: A field is not of its type.
`block_size` is not positive, or `init_weights` is not an accepted value.
`bias` asks for trained biases.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import C3AConfig
>>> config = C3AConfig(block_size=16, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"])
>>> config.block_size, config.peft_type
(16, <PeftType.C3A: 'C3A'>)
>>> C3AConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True

The adapter is built whole before the layer holds any of it.  A layer
that holds an adapter already keeps applying the adapters it applied:
the new one is inactive until `set_adapter` names it; a layer with
none starts applying this one.

Disabling a merged layer unmerges it first, here rather than on
the next call, so the forward pass never writes a weight — a

Whether the adapter takes part.  Gradient flags are left as

methods.summary: Apply the named adapters, and train exactly those unless `inference_mode`.
methods.extended:
The names this layer holds nothing for are skipped by the forward
pass.  A merged layer is unmerged first, since the active adapters
are no longer the merged ones.

parameters.name: adapter_names

methods.name: merge
methods.signature: merge(safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Fold the update into the base weights, in place.
methods.extended:
The weights keep their identity — they are written, not replaced —
so whatever holds them (an optimizer, a tied embedding) sees the
merged values.  That is also why a weight shared with another
module must not be merged into; the tuner's `merge_adapter` and
`merge_and_unload` refuse it, as this layer alone cannot see the
rest of the model.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description:
Check the merged weights for NaN / inf first and leave the base
untouched if there are any.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Adapters to merge; the active ones this layer holds by default.

raises.description:
An adapter name this layer does not hold, or `safe_merge`
found a non-finite merged weight.

The adapter is disabled, or the layer's own rules refuse the merge
(`lora_bias` on a base with no bias).
This layer's update cannot be written into its base weights.

methods.name: unmerge
methods.summary: Take every merged update back out of the base weights, in place.
methods.extended:
The result equals the original weights up to the rounding of the
round trip.

methods.name: supports_lora_conversion
methods.summary: Whether `adapter_name` on this layer can be converted to a plain LoRA update.

methods.name: in_features
methods.summary: Input features of the base layer.

methods.name: out_features
methods.summary: Output features of the base layer.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: The base layer's output plus every active adapter's contribution to it.
methods.extended:
The base output alone when adapters are disabled or merged; the sum is cast back to the
base output's dtype.

members.summary: Adapter bookkeeping and the kernel-to-update map shared by the C3A layers.
members.extended:
Per adapter: `c3a_kernel`, a `(d_out / b, d_in / b, b)` parameter, and the read-only
mapping `block_size`.  The forward pass adds each active adapter's circulant update
applied to the input (every adapter sees the layer's input); merging adds it to the weight.

parameters.name: base_layer
parameters.description: The module to adapt; kept as `base_layer`, its parameters shared.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter created at once.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The adapter's config (its `block_size` is this layer's).

raises.description: `base_layer` is not the module type the layer class adapts.

`config.block_size` does not divide the layer's input and output sizes, or
`base_layer` builds parameters on its first input.

members.name: Linear
members.signature: Linear(base_layer: nn.Module, adapter_name: str, config: C)
members.summary: An `nn.Linear` with a block-circulant update: $y = W x + b + \mathcal C(w)\,x / d_{in}$.

parameters.name: base_layer
parameters.description: The layer to adapt; the other parameters are those of `C3ALayer`.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter created at once.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The adapter's config (its `block_size` is this layer's).

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.c3a import C3AConfig, Linear
>>> base = nn.Linear(8, 4)
>>> layer = Linear(base, "default", C3AConfig(block_size=4, init_weights=True, target_modules=["x"]))
>>> tuple(layer.c3a_kernel["default"].shape)
(1, 2, 4)
>>> x = lucid.randn(2, 8)
>>> bool((layer(x) == base(x)).all().item())   # the kernels start at zero
True

methods.name: add_adapter
methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter starts frozen and inactive: the forward pass keeps
applying the adapters it applied, and every parameter keeps the
`requires_grad` it had.  `set_adapter` switches to it.  A
module an earlier adapter already wraps takes the new one beside
it; any other target is wrapped.  The model is left as it was if
the adapter cannot be added.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the new adapter; unique among the model's adapters.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how — the config class of this tuner's method.

raises.description:
The name is taken or malformed, the config is another
method's, no module matches it, or it cannot sit beside the
adapters held (two adapters training biases).
`config` is not an adapter config.

methods.name: set_adapter
methods.signature: set_adapter(adapter_name: str | list[str], inference_mode: bool = False)
methods.summary: Apply the named adapter(s) in the forward pass, and train exactly those.
methods.extended:
Every other adapter is frozen; the activated ones train unless
`inference_mode`.  A merged layer is unmerged first.  Layers that
hold none of the named adapters run their base alone.  The
parameters `bias` makes trainable follow the adapter that asked
for them.

raises.description:
A name is not one of the model's adapters, or two named
adapters train the same `modules_to_save` module.

raises.description: A name is not one of the model's adapters.

methods.name: delete_adapter
methods.summary: Remove an adapter: its parameters, its config, its `modules_to_save` copies.
methods.extended:
If it was active, the adapters still active stay so; when none
remain the first of the others (by name) takes over, with a
warning, and trains.  Deleting the last adapter leaves the layers
in the model, applying nothing; `unload()` removes them.

raises.description: The adapter does not exist, or it is merged — unmerge first.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Call the adapted model; its adapter layers do their work inside the call.

methods.name: merge_adapter
methods.signature: merge_adapter(adapter_names: list[str] | None = None, safe_merge: bool = False)
methods.summary: Fold adapter updates into their base weights, keeping the adapter layers.
methods.extended:
A merged model runs at the base model's cost; `unmerge_adapter`
takes the updates out again.  Every refusal is made before any
weight is written: nothing is merged if a layer's base weight is
shared with another module (a tied LM head — merging would change
that module too) or if the adapter is disabled.

parameters.description:
Adapters to merge; the active ones by default.  A layer holding
only some of them merges those.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description: Check every merged weight for NaN / inf before writing any.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or the adapter is
disabled (inside `disable_adapter()`).

A name is not one of the model's adapters, or `safe_merge`
found a non-finite merged weight.

methods.name: unmerge_adapter
methods.summary: Take every merged adapter update back out of its base weight.

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Merge the adapters into the base weights and return the plain model.
methods.extended:
Each adapter layer is replaced by its merged base module — the base
model's own module, holding its own `Parameter` objects — and each
`modules_to_save` entry by the active adapter's trained copy (the
original when that adapter has none).  Adapters not merged are
dropped with their layers.  Every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

parameters.name: progressbar
parameters.description: Accepted for the reference's signature; there is no progress bar.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description: Check every merged weight for NaN / inf before writing any.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Adapters to merge; the active ones by default.

returns.description: The model, merged, with no adapter layer left in it.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or a
`modules_to_save` module shared one (its trained copy would
break the tie).

methods.name: unload
methods.summary: Remove every adapter without merging and return the original model.
methods.extended:
Every adapter layer is replaced by the module it wrapped (a merged
one is unmerged first), every `modules_to_save` entry by its
original module, and every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

methods.name: enable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Apply the adapter again after `disable_adapter_layers`.

methods.name: disable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Run the base model alone: adapter updates off, original `modules_to_save`.

methods.name: supports_lora_conversion
methods.summary: Whether every adapted layer in this tuner supports conversion to LoRA.

members.summary: A model with C3A layers in it, and the tools to take them out again.
members.extended:
A module `config` selects becomes a `lucid.peft.tuners.c3a.Linear` around it
with a block-circulant update; everything else is frozen.  The model is edited in place
(reachable as `model`; public names this wrapper lacks are read from it) and
`peft_config` keeps `config` with the default targets spelled out.  A module's block
size is `block_size_pattern`'s entry for it, else `block_size`.  Adapters coexist
under names (`add_adapter`, `set_adapter`, `delete_adapter`).

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to adapt.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in every `c3a_kernel`.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

parameters.name: state_dict
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

raises.description:
`target_modules` selects nothing or a non-linear module, a block size does not
divide a module's sizes, or `modules_to_save` matches nothing.
Layers of another method are already in the model.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import C3AConfig, C3AModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(8, 2))
>>> c3a = C3AModel(net, C3AConfig(block_size=2, target_modules=["0"]), "default")
>>> tuple(net[0].c3a_kernel["default"].shape)
(4, 4, 2)
>>> net[0].base_layer.weight.requires_grad, net[0].c3a_kernel["default"].requires_grad
(False, True)
>>> c3a.unload() is net, type(net[0]) is nn.Linear
(True, True)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.c3a` — C3A: a block-circulant weight update applied by FFT.
extended:
C3A (Chen et al., 2024, [arXiv:2407.19342](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19342) — Circular Convolution Adaptation) cuts the update into
`block_size`-square blocks and makes each block a circulant, fixed by one kernel of length
`block_size`.  The layer trains those kernels, which give a high-rank update, and applies them by
FFT without building the matrix.  Pick it for a high-rank update with a parameter count set by
`block_size` instead of a rank.

Where the reference library keeps them, so `isinstance(m, C3ALayer)` and `from
lucid.peft.tuners.c3a import C3AConfig, Linear` read as they do there.  One layer type for the one
module the method adapts, `nn.Linear`.  `C3AConfig` and `C3AModel` are here and exported from
`lucid.peft`.  Importing the package registers the method (its config under `PeftType.C3A`, its
tuner and layer), which is what makes `get_peft_model` and `PeftModel.from_pretrained` know it.
citation: Chen, Aochuan, et al. "Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Circular Convolution." [arXiv:2407.19342](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19342), 2024.
theory:
C3A (Chen et al., 2024, [arXiv:2407.19342](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19342) — Circular Convolution Adaptation) makes the
weight update a **block-circulant matrix**: the $d_{out} \times d_{in}$ update is
cut into $b \times b$ blocks and each block is a circulant, fixed by its first row
— a length-$b$ kernel.  The layer trains $d_{out} d_{in} / b$ numbers
($b$ kernels per block row and column), which is high rank, and applies them by
FFT without building the matrix,

$$
